---
title: "Quiz · Pico Identity"
---

A short knowledge check. Answers are hidden behind callouts so you can
self-grade after answering.

## 1. What question does a DID answer that an ECI cannot?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
An ECI answers "how do I communicate with this Pico on this engine?" A DID
answers "which Pico is this?" — the durable identity of the Pico itself.
:::

## 2. What is the analogy for did:webvh and did:peer?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
A did:webvh is the Pico's **passport** (public identity for introduction);
a did:peer is a **private address given to one relationship**.
:::

## 3. Why does a Pico use a different did:peer for each relationship?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Isolation. If one relationship is compromised, its peer DID can be rotated,
removed, or recreated without changing the Pico's other relationships, and
no single relationship can reveal the others.
:::

## 4. Which DID is primarily an introduction identity?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
The **did:webvh**. It is used for public identification, resolution, and
cryptographic introduction, not for every subsequent interaction.
:::
